name: misfire
description: Use when a petrol engine shakes, misfires, idles rough, the MIL flashes or P0300-P0304 is stored: misfire counts per cylinder from Mode 06.
instructions: Call run_skill {"name":"misfire"}: it reads the Mode 06 misfire monitors (MID A2-A5 = cylinders 1-4) and tells one bad cylinder from misfires spread across the engine.
Open fault_codes for P0300 (random) and P0301-P0304 (cylinder 1-4); open sensor_tests for the other Mode 06 results when it is offered.
With spread misfires, run fuel_trims when it is offered: a lean mixture misfires on every cylinder.
When the car reports no counts, say misfires could not be counted: the monitor may not have run since the codes were cleared.
interpret: One cylinder with 5 or more misfires and at least twice the next highest: look at that cylinder's coil, plug, injector and compression (swap its coil with a neighbour's to see whether the misfire follows).
Misfires spread across cylinders (10 or more in total): a shared cause such as a vacuum leak or lean mixture, low fuel pressure, EGR, worn plugs all round or the LPG mixture.
Counts cover the latest driving cycles; a cold engine or a rough road can add a few counts without a fault.
A flashing MIL means misfires bad enough to damage the catalytic converter: drive gently and have it checked soon.
